models.inverse_notes: Target d: known D>=0 and w>0 give d=D/w, uniquely, with original contexts and guards. Check D=0.000125 kg and w=12.5 kg gives d=0.00001 and forward D=0.000125. D=0 gives d=0 and is admitted as the stated arithmetic boundary. Target w: known D and d>0 give w=D/d and require w>0 (hence D>0). If d=0 and D=0 every positive w satisfies the identity; if d=0 and D>0 none does. This is algebraic inversion of an amount definition, not identification of an appropriate clinical weight or coefficient.
limitations: A daily or continuous-rate prescription has different temporal semantics and cannot be bound to d unchanged.
No maximum-dose, renal, obesity, neonatal, pregnancy or route-specific adjustment is established; the source's illustrative drug orders are numerical examples, not reusable defaults.

relationship.original_equation: eClcr = {((140-age) x weight)/(72 SCr)} x 0.85 if female, with eClcr in mL/min, age in years, weight in kg and SCr in mg/dL
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced C maps to eClcr, a to age's numerical value in years, w to weight, and sCr to SCr. Introduced z is 0 for the source male branch or 1 for its female branch; 1-0.15*z exactly encodes the published 15% reduction, not a fitted continuous sex factor. Age is a numerical year index (unit years, dimensionless in this snapshot), not an elapsed-time input converted to seconds. Serum creatinine is kg/m^3, so 1 mg/dL=0.01 kg/m^3. The source denominator coefficient 72 kg*min*dL/(mg*mL) becomes 432000000000 s in coherent units. With w in the runtime mass base and sCr on the same mass scale, mass cancels and C is m^3/s. Dimensions: (1)*(1)*M/(T*(M L^-3))=L^3 T^-1. The normalized 432000000000 is the dimensional empirical coefficient, not an extra input/output unit conversion. Unit scales alone must convert future mL/min display ports. Unambiguous NKF extracted equation is the authority; original PDF visual inspection was unavailable, so no full-original methods/table inspection is claimed.

relationship.original_equation: Creatinine Clearance = ((total urine volume / collection time) x urine creatinine) / blood creatinine
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced U maps to urine creatinine, P to blood/serum creatinine, V to total urine volume and t to collection time. Both concentrations must be of creatinine on the same mass basis. Source mg/dL concentrations are normalized to kg/m^3, volume to m^3 and duration to seconds; no conversion literal is inlined. Source's reported 168.3 mL/min is retained as the oracle after conversion; no BSA indexing is in this equation. The no-excretion U=0 limit is admitted algebraically for a positive collected sample; zero collected volume is excluded because an assayed urine specimen is required.

models.inverse_notes: Target D: V>=0, H>0, Q>0 give D=V*H/Q uniquely. Check V=7.5e-6 m^3, H=0.0004 kg, Q=5e-6 m^3 gives D=0.0006 kg and forward V=7.5e-6. V=0 gives D=0 uniquely. Target H: D>0, Q>0, V>0 give H=D*Q/V>0. Target Q: D>0, H>0, V>0 give Q=V*H/D>0. Retain original guards and formulation context. With D=V=0, H and Q remain underdetermined positive values; with D=0,V>0 there is no solution. With D>0,V=0 no finite positive H,Q can satisfy the identity. Inverting does not authorize changing a prescription or stock formulation.
limitations: Does not select a dose, stock strength, dilution, syringe or rounding policy; no clinical limits are inferred from educational examples.
Cannot use bulk solution density for H/Q, or use added diluent volume as final stock volume when reconstitution changes volume.

relationship.original_equation: Desired Amount / Dose on hand x Volume = Dose (liquid quantity)
relationship.translation_notes: Preserve source D and H; introduced Q renames the source stock Volume to avoid collision with introduced output V (source liquid Dose). D,H are active-drug mass in kg, Q,V liquid volume in m^3. Normalize mg to kg and mL to m^3 before reference entry; expression D*Q/H has no conversion coefficient. Dimensions: M*L^3/M=L^3; runtime mass scale cancels. H/Q is constituent active-drug mass concentration, not bulk solution density: the building-energy inventory's generic density relationship concerns total substance mass and is not a compatible unqualified binding. Tablet counts are treated as an alternate desired-over-have profile in deferred notes, not another record created solely by unit spelling.

sources.evidence: Scales labeled liquid volume by desired mass relative to labeled mass; example gives 0.5 mL and another gives 0.75 mL.

models.summary: Converts an already specified active-drug mass into the corresponding volume of one labeled liquid formulation. It is a proportional amount identity; neither choosing an amount nor deciding to administer it is included.
models.title: Liquid medication volume from prescribed mass and labeled strength

variables.context: Same independently authorized single administration, active drug/moiety and homogeneous liquid stock at its labeled concentration. The supplied reference mass H and volume Q describe the same final formulation. Source is nursing calculation education, not age-specific drug validation; patient eligibility and prescription appropriateness are external.
variables.definition: Active-drug mass already specified for this single administration on the same labeled active-moiety basis as H.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; zero is the no-amount arithmetic boundary, not a prescribed therapy.
